# Rasa MCP Server

MCP server for building, validating, training, and testing Rasa assistants.

This server enables AI agents to:
<!-- engine:calm -->
- Inspect project structure (flows, slots, responses, actions)
<!-- /engine -->
- Validate configuration and training data
- Train models
- Test conversations and debug assistant behavior
- Simulate goal-driven conversations and evaluate outcomes

<!-- engine:calm -->
## Introspection

List and get flows, slots, responses, and actions.

- `list_project_flow_definitions` - List all flows in the project
- `list_project_slot_definitions` - List all slots in the domain
- `list_project_response_definitions` - List all responses in the domain
- `get_flow` - Get a single flow by ID or name with full definition
- `get_slot` - Get a single slot by name with full definition
- `get_response` - Get a single response by name with full definition
- `list_project_custom_actions_in_domain` - List custom actions declared in domain
- `list_custom_action_implementations` - List custom action implementations from Python files
- `list_default_action_names` - List built-in Rasa actions

## Schemas

Get official Rasa schemas for validation and code generation.

- `get_flow_schema` - Flow JSON Schema (for flows.yml structure)
- `get_domain_schema` - Domain YAML schema (slots, actions, responses structure within the domain files)
- `get_e2e_schema` - Assistant E2E test YAML schema (test cases and steps)

<!-- /engine -->
<!-- engine:mantle -->
## Mantle projects

This is a Mantle (skills-based) agent: `agent.yml`, `integrations.yml`, and one `skills/<id>/skill.md` per skill, plus optional files such as `memory.yml` and `responses.yml`. It has no flows, slots, or domain files, so the flow, slot, response, action, and schema tools, which read those CALM files, are not offered. Responses are still supported: define them in `responses.yml`, project-wide or per skill.

- `validate_project` checks the whole project, including every skill, memory, and responses
- `train_rasa_assistant` packages the project into a model archive under `models/`

For authoring guidance, use the installed Mantle agent skills and the Mantle docs in `.rasa/docs/mantle/` (fetch them with `rasa tools init docs mantle`).

<!-- /engine -->
## Build

Validate project and train models.

- `validate_project` - Check configuration and training data for errors
- `train_rasa_assistant` - Train a new model

Always validate before training. Fix any validation errors before proceeding.

## Test

Talk to assistant, get logs, and inspect tracker state.

- `talk_to_assistant` - Send messages and get responses
- `get_assistant_logs` - View recent logs for troubleshooting

Use these to verify your changes work as expected.

## Evaluation

Simulate goal-driven conversations and score outcomes against assertions and criteria.

- `validate_scenario` - Validate scenario YAML syntax, assertions, and slot references before running
- `evaluate_agent` - Run LLM-simulated multi-turn evaluation over one or more scenarios; writes results to `eval/results/<experiment_timestamp>/`

Requires a running Rasa server (`rasa run --inspect`), `eval/conftest.yml`, and scenario files in `eval/scenarios/`. Always call `validate_scenario` before `evaluate_agent`, and pass all of a session's scenarios to it in one call — `scenario_paths` is a list, runs go concurrently, and they share one summary. Each `scenario_results` entry gives `runs_passed`/`runs_total` for the verdict, plus `runs_errored` for runs that failed for harness reasons — a timeout, a cancellation, or an error captured during the run — rather than on their merits. Evaluation starts each conversation with `/session_start` (welcome first when configured), then `initial_slots`, then simulated turns over REST (`?stream=true`; a classic JSON-array body on that request is parsed in place). Results are `eval/results/<timestamp>/<scenario>/run_N.txt` plus `run_N.json`. Set `show_tracker_events=true` to add important tracker events, grouped by user turn, to each `run_N.txt` report when diagnosing where a conversation went off track. This option is off by default and does not change pass/fail. To author scenarios interactively, use the **simulate conversation** skill (`rasa-simulating-conversations`) — it can generate scenario YAML from goals, criteria, and assertions, then validate before you run `evaluate_agent`.
